lines: A bad omen once sent everyone indoors. The storm passed, but the soup burned.
I made a remedy so bitter the patient recovered out of spite.
One winter the bottles froze before the well did. We learned to move the shelves.
A farmer mistook purple smoke for a curse. It was beetroot in the wrong pot.
I once stayed awake all night for a fever that broke at sunrise.
The bell rang during a brewing lesson, and half the bottles survived the panic.
A child brought me a wounded chicken and watched every bandage I tied.
We spent three days fearing a strange noise under the chapel. It was a cat.
A traveler paid for a tonic with a story about an ocean monument.
I saw lightning strike the same fence twice. We moved the fence.
The first potion I brewed alone stained my hands for a week.
A golem once stood outside my door until its cracked arm was repaired.
Someone left flowers by the brewing stand after a hard recovery.
During one raid, we hid the medicine under sacks of potatoes.
I treated a woodcutter who apologized to the tree before every swing.
An old villager taught me to warm bandages by the stove in winter.
A supposed curse vanished when we cleaned the village well.
I lost a whole shelf to one loose cat and one open window.
The strangest omen I ever saw was silence at midday. Everyone was fishing.
A merchant once traded me a bottle that hummed. I never opened it.
